cards.front: Recall a key point about Minerals & Their Properties
cards.back: A mineral is a naturally occurring, inorganic solid with a definite chemical composition and crystalline structure

cards.front: Recall a key point about Minerals & Their Properties
cards.back: Silicates (containing SiO4 tetrahedra) are the most common mineral group, making up ~90% of Earth's crust

cards.front: Recall a key point about Minerals & Their Properties
cards.back: Key properties for mineral identification: hardness (Mohs scale 1-10), cleavage, fracture, lustre, colour, streak, density and crystal habit

cards.front: Recall a key point about Minerals & Their Properties
cards.back: Common rock-forming minerals: quartz, feldspar, mica, calcite, olivine, pyroxene, amphibole

cards.front: Recall a key point about Minerals & Their Properties
cards.back: Hardness is measured on the Mohs scale: talc (1) to diamond (10); each mineral can scratch those below it

cards.front: Recall a key point about Minerals & Their Properties
cards.back: Cleavage is the tendency of a mineral to break along flat planes of weakness in its crystal structure

cards.front: What should you know about gcse geology exam tips — minerals & their properties?
cards.back: 1. For Minerals & Their Properties questions, use correct geological terminology and classify features precisely 2. Reference specific geological time periods and processes 3. When interpreting data, consider the quality and limitations of the evidence 4. Apply your understanding of Minerals & Their Properties to fieldwork observations and map data 5. For evaluation, weigh competing geological theories with evidence
Describe the physical properties used to identify minerals and explain why multiple properties are needed. [6 marks]

AO1 (Knowledge & Understanding): Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of minerals & their properties, including key geological concepts, observational data and theoretical models relevant to OCR J357. AO2 (Application of Knowledge): Apply knowledge and understanding of minerals & their properties to both familiar and unfamiliar geological contexts, using field evidence and theoretical principle
